chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Barqī, from his father, from the one whom he mentioned, from Rufayd, the mawla of Yazīd ibn ‘Amr ibn Hubayrah, who said:

Ibn Hubayrah became angry with me and swore that he would surely kill me. So I fled from him and sought refuge with Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, and I informed him of my situation. He said to me: “Go back, and convey to him my greetings, and say to him: I have granted protection over your mawla Rufayd, so do not assail him with evil.” So I said to him: “May I be made your ransom, he is a Syrian of corrupt opinion.” He said: “Go to him just as I am telling you.” So I went.

When I was in some of the open desert lands, a Bedouin met me and said: “Where are you going? I see the face of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Stretch out your hand.” So I did, and he said: “The hand of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Show your leg.” So I showed my leg, and he said: “The leg of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Show your body.” So I did, and he said: “The body of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Bring out your tongue.” So I did, and he said to me: “Proceed, for there is no harm upon you, for in your tongue there is a message; if you were to bring it to the lofty mountains, they would submit to you.”

He said: So I came until I stood at the door of Ibn Hubayrah and asked permission. When I entered upon him, he said: “His own legs have brought the traitor to you. Boy, bring the execution mat and the sword.” Then he gave orders concerning me, so I was bound and my head was fastened, and the executioner stood over me to strike my neck. So I said: “O Amīr, you did not seize me by force; rather, I came to you of my own accord, and here is a matter that I will mention to you, then after that you may do as you wish.”

He said: “Speak.” I said: “Let me be alone with you.” So he ordered those present, and they left. Then I said to him: “Ja‘far ibn Muhammad conveys to you his greetings and says to you: I have granted protection over your mawla Rufayd, so do not assail him with evil.” He said: “By Allah, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad truly said these words to you and conveyed greetings to me?” So I swore to him, and he made me repeat it three times. Then he untied my shoulders and said: “I will not be satisfied with you until you do to me what I did to you.” I said: “My hand will not proceed to do that, nor is my soul pleased with it.” He said: “By Allah, nothing will satisfy me except that.” So I did to him as he had done to me, and I released him. Then he handed me his seal and said: “My affairs are in your hand, so manage them as you wish.”

key_terms.السَّلَامَ: greeting of peace conveyed from the Imam
key_terms.خَاتَمَهُ: his seal, symbolizing delegated control over affairs

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq عليه السلام protect Rufayd from Ibn Hubayrah?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Rufayd sought refuge with Imam Ja‘far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام after Ibn Hubayrah threatened to kill him. By the Imam’s message of protection, the ruler’s anger was transformed into submission and trust, showing the authority and effect of the Imam’s word.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Rufeyd, a slave of Yazeed Bin Amro Bin Hubeyra who said,

‘Ibn Ubeyra was angry upon me and swore against me that he would kill me. So I fled from him and sought refuge with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I let him know of my compulsion. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Leave, and convey the greetings to him from me<sup>asws</sup>, and say to him that I<sup>asws</sup> have undertook upon you (to protect) your slave Rufeyd, therefore do not approach him with evil’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! He is a Syrian, of bad views’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go to him just as I<sup>asws</sup> am saying to you’. So I returned.

When I was in one of the valleys, a Bedouin faced me and he said, ‘Where are you going? I see a face of a killed one’. Then he said to me, ‘Bring out your hand’. So I did, and he said, ‘A hand of a killed one’. Then he said to me, ‘Bring forward your leg’. So I brought my leg forward, and he said, ‘A leg of a killed one’. Then he said to me, ‘Bring forward your body towards me’. So I did, and he said, ‘A body of a killed one’. Then he said to me, ‘Bring out your tongue’. So I did, and he said to me, ‘Carry on, for there is no evil upon you, for in your tongue is a message. If you were to go with it to the tall mountain, it would be in obedience to you’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went until I paused upon the door of Ibn Hubeyra and sought permission. When I came over to him, he said, ‘The traitor comes over on his own legs. O slave! (Bring me) the leather cords and the sword!’ Then he ordered with me, so I was bound and my head held tight, and the swordsman stood over me to strike my neck off. So I said, ‘O you Emir! You did not overcome me by force, and rather I came over to you from my own self, and over here there is a matter I want to mention to you, then it would be you and your business (whatever you want to do)’.

He said, ‘Speak’. So I said, ‘Isolate with me’. He instructed the ones present, and they went out, and I said to him, ‘Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> conveys the greetings to you and is saying to you: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> have undertaken upon you, your slave Rufeyda, therefore do no approach him with evil’. So he said, ‘By Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said these words to you, and conveyed the greetings to me?’ So I swore on oath to him, and he reiterated it thrice upon me. Then he freed my ropes, then said, ‘I will not be content from you until you do with me what I did with you’. I said, ‘My hand will not go with (doing) that, nor will my self be good with it’. So he said, ‘By Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! I will not be contented except with that’. So I did with him just as he had done with me and I untied him. So he gave me his seal and said, ‘My affairs are in your hands, therefore manage these as you so desire to’.
en.sarwar: 2. Certain persons of our people have narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father from Sulayman ibn Sama‘a from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Qasim from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following.
“Once abu Ja‘far al-Mansur ordered his governor of Makka and Madina, al-Hassan ibn al-Zayd, to set fire to the house of Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) to burn him to death.
The house of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) was set on fire and it burned the door and the corridor.
Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) came out walking in the fire and stepping on it and would say, ‘I am the son of ’A‘raq al-Thara (’Isma‘il), I am the son of Ibrahim, (Abraham) the beloved friend of Allah.”
